newsitem.title: USA: CNS Q1 sales hurt by retail inventory cuts.
newsitem.headline: CNS Q1 sales hurt by retail inventory cuts.

text.p: CNS Inc on Monday said its first-quarter sales fell to $19.4 million from $20.8 million in the year-earlier period primarily because retailers reduced their inventories of its Breather Right nasal strip.

"Although consumer purchases increased, retailers ordered from the company approximately 20 percent fewer strips than were sold at retail during the first two months of the quarter," CNS chief executive Daniel Cohen said in a news release.
Breathe Right said that, based on the most recent data, it believes consumer purchases rose 15 percent from last year in the first eight weeks of the quarter.

"While our sales to retailers declined, our marketing and selling costs increased nearly 50 percent because we spent more on advertising with the aim of increasing consumer trial of the product," Cohen said. "New trial during the quarter increased by approximately 1.5 million U.S. households to a cumulative total of 10.5 million."
CNS said it is looking for trials to get a boost from a new promotion with Tylenol PM and a joint promotion to coincide with the August scheduled release of the movie "Leave It to Beaver."
The company reported net income of $1.3 million, or $0.07 a share in the first quarter, compared with $3.1 million, or $0.17 a share a year ago.
